question.worked_solution:
We start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 \\ 6 & 3 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 6 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & 8 \\ -9 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 6 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to basis vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the reduced matrix has $2$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $2$ non-zero rows). 

Therefore, the dimension of the span is $2.$
